title: Structured data processing — JSON-like records, malformed rows

aiGuide.intro: Build the model, parse JSON-ish lines, aggregate — and treat a bad line as **data, not an exception**. The follow-up is a file that does not fit in memory.
plan: Ask: what makes a line bad? what is reported? does one bad line stop the batch?
Model: Event record + Reject reasons; one test line per reason
AI writes the parser and aggregator against your model → review → run
AI adds more malformed cases with reasons; you check them
1 GB file: AI reviews memory; you prove a single pass
Follow-ups: HyperLogLog for distinct users, schema evolution

stages.name: Parse, model, aggregate
stages.yours: Model first: `Event(User, Action, Ts, Ms)` and the `Reject` reasons. The rule: **a bad line is counted under exactly one reason and never stops the batch**. Write five bad lines, one per reason, and three good ones.
stages.ai: **Co-generate** the parser: System.Text.Json plumbing is boilerplate. The reasons and the accumulator are yours.
bad: Parse these JSON lines and aggregate by action, skipping bad lines.
A `try/catch` around the **whole loop** — the first bad line ends parsing — or a catch-all that skips silently with no count.
"Skipping" hides data loss: nothing counted, nothing reported
No reasons, so you cannot test each one
good: Write Aggregator.Consume(IEnumerable<string> lines): parse each line with System.Text.Json. Skip blank lines. Count each bad line in Rejected under exactly one Reject reason: NotJson, NotAnObject, MissingField, WrongType (user/action not a non-empty string; ts/ms not an integer), OutOfRange (ms < 0). One bad line must never stop the rest. Per action keep count, sum and max of ms, and distinct users. Summary sorted by count desc then action (ordinal); mean as a double. Keep my Event record and Reject enum. Show only Aggregator.
stages.reply: Typical defect (verified planted flaw R7): **try/catch around the whole loop** — 4 lines with the 2nd bad → 1 parsed, silently.
validate: One line per reason — each counted once, under the right reason
A bad line in the middle: lines after it still counted
stages.fix: Whole-loop try/catch → **a narrow follow-up**: "Move the try/catch inside the loop so each line is handled on its own; count the failure under NotJson and continue."
stages.say: "A bad line is data, not an exception. One malformed record must not lose the next million."
stages.require: Implement `Aggregator.Consume` and `Summary`. Count each rejected line under exactly one `Reject` reason; never throw on bad input.
stages.say_iv: Here is a log of JSON-like events, one per line. Build the classes, and give me per-action counts and latency stats. Some lines are garbage.

stages.name: The file is 1 GB
stages.yours: Say the constraint: **one pass over an IEnumerable, aggregates only**. Then say what still grows: the set of distinct users per action (→ a HyperLogLog sketch at scale).
stages.ai: **AI reviews** — ask for a memory review, not new code.
bad: Make it handle a 1 GB file.
`File.ReadAllLines` "to load it efficiently", or `lines.ToList()` so it can count first — the whole file in memory.
It optimises the wrong thing (speed of loading, not memory)
good: Review Consume for memory on a 1 GB input. It must enumerate the lines exactly once and keep only per-action aggregates. List everything that grows with the input, most significant first. Do not rewrite the code. The Aggregator is pasted below. No ToList, no ReadAllLines. Explain why each item grows. Keep my code as it is.
**"Do not rewrite"** keeps it a review
stages.reply: A good reply names the per-action HashSet of users as the only thing that grows. A bad one suggests `.ToList()` or a `.Count()` before the loop — a second enumeration.
validate: Enumerated exactly once — count enumerations in the test
Only aggregates kept; distinct users is the one growing set
stages.say: "One pass, aggregates only. The only thing that grows is distinct users — at scale that becomes a HyperLogLog sketch, about 1.6% error in 12 KB."
stages.require: `Consume` must enumerate its input exactly once and must not buffer it. The test streams 300,000 generated lines through an enumerable that throws if read twice.
stages.say_iv: What happens if the input is a 1 GB file? Can you process it without loading everything into memory?

checklist: Which method, in which class — paste your class
Implement Log in the Logger class below
Every rule in one sentence, the boundary included
Keep my fields; no new public members
The wrong answers you expect, by name
No DateTime, no timers, no ConcurrentDictionary
Ask for assumptions first, or a reason per test
List your assumptions before the code
Keep the reply small enough to review
Show only Log · change only that line

none: You think and write. This is what is scored.
check: Ask it to attack your design or maths — no code.
cogen: Your design, pasted; the AI fills in mechanical code you can verify fast.
tests: Boilerplate you can check: ask for a reason per expected value.
review: A second reader for a named class of bug — "do not rewrite".
